lean.annotation: The proof first bounds the measured program’s action using an average of its two corrected branch operators at each measurement. These lower bounds compose through the circuit. lean.name: RealizesCleanSubroutine
lean.plain: Hoare specification with zero ancillas at entry and return
lean.annotation: `RealizesCleanSubroutine` forms its postcondition from an arbitrary observable and restricts it to zero ancillas. The `qAssign` in the precondition pulls that observable back through the target unitary. A second restriction imposes zero ancillas at entry, so the triple specifies both the data action and the final state of the workspace.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.arcsin_correctness
lean.plain: Uniform approximation and exact modular addition
lean.annotation: The conclusion uses `RealizesCleanSubroutine` with the unitary `arcsinTableUnitary z`. It specifies the operation obtained by linear extension of the modular addition on basis states, after initializing the ancillas to zero. The width and tolerance assumptions are $k\ge3$ and at least half a grid step.

lean.name: QuantumComputation.Specs.ArcsinImpl.realizesCleanSubroutine_compileList102
lean.plain: Clean unitary action from the phase-aware basis calculation
lean.annotation: The same basis outputs can carry different relative phases. If two clean basis inputs pick up opposite signs, their sum becomes a difference of the two intended outputs. The `phaseList102 … = false` clause fixes the phase at $+1$ for every clean basis input. The proof then compares the operators on basis vectors with the zero-ancilla projector.
